chunks: 8 - He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali Majilawayh narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn 'Atiyyah, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his progeny, said:
“Death is an expiation for the sins of the believers.”

key_terms.المؤمنين: the believers — those who have faith in God and His message
key_terms.الموت: death — the inevitable end of worldly life
key_terms.كفارة: expiation, atonement — an act or event that removes sins

ai.seo_question: Is death an expiation for the sins of believers in Islam?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition conveys that death itself serves as an expiation (kaffara) for the sins of believers. In Islamic theology, this hadith provides comfort to the faithful by affirming that the experience of death purifies the believer from accumulated sins. The hadith was transmitted through Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq from the Prophet Muhammad himself.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 8. He said: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to me from Muhammad ibn ‘Ali Majilawayh from his uncle Mohammad ibn Abul Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, that: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:
"Death is an expiateon for the sins of the believers."
